subject: Next steps: Nebula AI competitive bake-off & hyperscaler comparison
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@nebula.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.o@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + immediate next steps after today's discovery call

Alex — thanks for a great conversation earlier. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so we remain aligned: 

- Goal (what we heard): Run a 2-week competitive bake-off comparing Redwood inference vs Nebula's preferred hyperscaler-managed inference and one other API for latency, cost, and 95th/99th tail under production traffic shape.
- Success criteria (draft): average p99 latency < 350ms for 2k tokens, cost per 1k tokens <= $X (we'll finalize), functional parity on zero-shot QA and structured extraction (F1 > 0.82).
- Tests we propose: throughput ramp (10 -> 1,000 rps), cold-start latency, KV cache efficiency for chat histories, quantization impact on quality, and failover behavior across regions.

What I'd like from you by EOD Wed: confirm which hyperscaler they're most interested in (GCP/AWS/Azure), provide a small sample of your real production prompt mixes (anonymized), and identify the procurement/regulatory contacts for PO timeline.

Attached I'm sharing a short playbook with test cases and an initial timeline. Connor will own the test harness; Rishi will be on-call for SLA and perf questions. I'll coordinate the schedule with your team.

Thanks,

— Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.c@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0193
Redwood Inference — production-first LLM inference

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-playbook.xlsx (test matrix), redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.pdf (comparative notes)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@nebula.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sana Patel <sana.patel@nebula.ai>, Procurement Ops <procure@nebula.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + immediate next steps after today's discovery call

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Hyperscaler: Nebula prefers starting with GCP endpoints (we have committed spend there). If results are good we'll add AWS for a follow-up comparison.
- Prompt mixes: I can send an anonymized sample later today. Expect ~60% conversational QA, 30% structured extraction (invoices/POs), 10% embeddings/rerank.
- Procurement: looping in Procurement Ops (procure@nebula.ai) — PO process typically 3–4 weeks after SOW.

Quick questions: can Redwood run the quantized model variants (8-bit) and still provide per-token cost reporting? Also want to see KV cache effectiveness for long chat contexts (10–20k tokens).

On timing: Wed — I confirm GCP + sample prompts. Would prefer the 2-week window to start the week of May 25 if that works for Redwood.

— Alex
Head of Product, Nebula AI
alex.j@nebula.ai | +1 (718) 555-4822

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@nebula.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.o@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.m@redwood.ai>, Procurement Ops <procure@nebula.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + immediate next steps after today's discovery call

Thanks Alex — that's perfect. A few concrete items we can lock today: 

1) Test variants: Yes — we'll run full precision (fp16), 8-bit quantization, and a trimmed performance-oriented variant. We'll include per-token accounting in the logs and a post-run cost sheet.

2) KV/cache tests: we'll simulate 10k–20k token histories; Connor will instrument cache hit-rate and tail latency by prefix length.

3) Timeline & owners:
   - May 18: Redwood infra readiness check and credentials exchange (owner: Marissa)
   - May 20: Test harness deployed in Nebula staging (owner: Connor)
   - May 25–Jun 7: 2-week bake-off window (owner: Connor + Alex point of contact)
   - Jun 9: Results review + decision call (owner: Marissa)

4) Success criteria (working draft):
   - Perf: p99 < 350ms for conversational 2k token median payload under 500 rps steady-state
   - Cost: Redwood cost per 1k tokens <= hyperscaler baseline by at least 10% (finalized after initial run)
   - Quality: structured extraction F1 delta <= 0.03 vs hyperscaler baseline for the same model family

Attached again is the playbook with test cases. We'll also share a small harness container and Connor will provide runbook steps.

Connor — I'll need a quick checklist from you for the staging deploy (credentials, IP allowlist, test dataset location).

Alex / Procurement — if PO timing looks like 3–4 weeks post-SOW, we'll plan the engagement agreements accordingly. Happy to provide an SOW template.

Cheers,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-playbook.xlsx, sample-kv-cache-logs.tar.gz

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.m@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.o@redwood.ai>, Alex Johnson <alex.j@nebula.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + immediate next steps after today's discovery call

Looping in some technical guardrails from the infra side. A few notes for the bake-off engineers: 

- Metrics to capture (minimum): per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), token throughput, GPU utilization, VRAM footprint, KV cache hit-rate by prefix size, and model quantization impact on perplexity / downstream F1.
- Logging: we will provide structured JSON logs and a small post-processing script to normalize per-token cost across providers. Please ensure Nebula can host an SFTP drop for logs or provide a read-only GCS bucket.
- Failover tests: we'll run a simulated region outage for 30s and verify model fallback latency and correctness. Expect temporary error spikes; we will capture re-play traces.
- Security: all data in flight will use mutual TLS for the proxy; we will redact PII in any sample prompts you provide and sign an NDA addendum if required.

Connor — please confirm the container image tag and runbook links you plan to use. I'll prep the dashboards (Grafana + short Loki scrape) and a perf checklist to hand off to Nebula.

— Rishi
Director, Applied ML Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@nebula.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sana Patel <sana.patel@nebula.ai>, Procurement Ops <procure@nebula.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.o@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + immediate next steps after today's discovery call

Thanks team — this looks good and actionable. Confirmations from Nebula: 

- We will provide anonymized prompt mixes by EOD Wed (May 14).
- GCP only for the first run. We can provide a read-only GCS bucket for logs; procurement confirms PO cadence and we'll aim to sign the SOW by June 1.
- Timeline: May 18 infra check OK with our infra team; May 25 start date for the 2-week window is acceptable.

Action owners acknowledged:
- Credentials & infra readiness: Marissa
- Harness deployment + run: Connor
- Perf dashboards & metric capture: Rishi
- Procurement & SOW: Procurement Ops / Sana Patel

We'll expect the Redwood team to share the final SOW template and the first-pass cost sheet before May 18 so Procurement can review. Looking forward to the test.

Best,
Alex
Head of Product, Nebula AI
